# lean-pkg comparator coverage

read-only: the claims covered by the comparator configuration tracked at the gate-bound commit, and why a changed one needs a new gate (`comparator config --coverage NAME` is the same).

Also spelled: `lean-pkg comparator config --coverage NAME` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg comparator coverage [--json] NAME
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `comparator coverage NAME` | read-only: at the gate-bound commit (the recorded gate receipt's commit), how many theorem/lemma claims the comparator configuration tracked there covers, does not cover, or lists only as scaffold TODO (definitions and superseded claims are not compared); names any configuration changed since then (working tree, uncommitted, untracked, committed after the gate) with the candidate's counts shown apart, never substituted; states that a changed or uncommitted config cannot certify the bound tree and a new gate at a commit that tracks it is required; ends with the exact next commands. Exit 0; no gate receipt is a refusal (exit 1) | `[--json]` (`bound_commit`, `covered`, `not_covered`, `todo`, `uncovered[]`, `config_changed`, `changed_configs[]`, `candidate`, `statement`, `next_commands[]`) |

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `comparator-coverage` (exit 0): `bound_commit`, `candidate`, `changed_configs`, `claims_source`, `config_changed`, `configs`, `covered`, `head`, `hints`, `judged_as_problems`, `name`, `next_commands`, `not_applicable`, `not_covered`, `ok`, `statement`, `theorem_claims`, `todo`, `uncovered`

## Examples

Which claims the comparator configuration at the gate-bound commit covers, and which it does not.

```bash
lean-pkg comparator coverage my-proof
```
